thread:
sam: FYI — follow-up from last night's tail-latency incident. TL;DR: KV cache stampede + a networking flake caused sustained p95 breaches on /embed during a 30m window. We burned ~22% of the monthly error budget for that route. Need to track remediation owners, put temporary SLO adjustments in place, and tighten dashboards so we catch recurrence earlier.
jin: On it. I can own the infra remediation (cache backpressure + retry budget). Planning to: 1) add token bucket limiting for upstream calls, 2) add per-worker concurrency cap, 3) test in canary. ETA: proposal PR by EOD.
marie: I'll own observability. Action items: add live KV miss rate, per-route error-budget burn-rate, and a p99 heatmap to the SLO dashboard. Will also add an alert for sustained p95 > 400ms for 10m on /embed. PR by tomorrow morning.
sam: For the temporary SLO change, propose scoped change only for /embed: raise P95 SLO from 350ms -> 600ms for a 72h window starting at rollout. Rationale: avoid noisy paging while we validate infra fix. We should have an automatic rollback of the SLO change if burn rate exceeds 2x during the window. Thoughts?
leo: Small thumbs up. Prefer we document the exact rollback predicate: if burn-rate > 200% for a rolling 15m, revert SLO change and trigger paging. Also prefer shorter window (48h) unless we need more time.
jin: Agree on rollback predicate. 48h sounds fine if canary results look good. I'll instrument a canary job that runs synthetic requests vs known vectors to measure p95/p99 pre/post.
marie: Note: there's a recurring pattern with network retries spiking during autoscaler events. I'll link the trace we saw in the postmortem. That suggests adding a tracing tag for autoscaler events on the dashboard.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0316-07 created and linked to postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2026-03-16-tail-latency-embed
sam: Owner recap: jin -> infra PR + canary orchestration; marie -> dashboards/alerts & trace tags; leo -> SLO change approver + rollback monitor; sam -> SLO change doc + compliance request + schedule sync.
marie: I'll include KV miss breakdown by model in the dashboard to help identify hot keys. Also adding a burn-rate timeseries panel for the month.
jin: Commands I ran early this morning, paste:
```
# check miss rates
curl -s http://metrics.internal/kv/miss_rate?route=embed | jq .
# list recent autoscaler events
kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector involvedObject.kind=HorizontalPodAutoscaler
```
jin: Found bursts of retries coinciding with pod churn; average retry count jumped from 1.2 -> 4.8 during rolling updates. Will try to stagger scale events and add backpressure.
leo: Thanks. For the SLO change flow: I'll need the SLO doc (sam), the canary dashboard link, and the exact rollback predicate. Once I get that I'll approve and notify SRE oncall.
sam: Filing SLO change now. Schedule: proposal PR by EOD, dashboard PR tomorrow AM, staging canary within 24h, prod rollout + SLO window tied to successful canary. Sync at 16:30 UTC to review canary results.
marie: ping me on reviews, will prioritize. :eyes:
jin: starting infra tests now. will post updates here. :hammer_and_wrench:
ops-bot: Canary safety note: auto-rollback enabled. If p95 > 650ms for >10m during canary, deploy will rollback automatically.
sam: Great. Quick checklist for thread: [jin] infra PR & canary orchestration, [marie] dashboard & alerts PR, [leo] SLO approval + rollback monitor, [sam] SLO doc + sync scheduling. We'll reconvene after canary run.
